Time an expression

Source: R/timer.R
timer.Rd

Evaluate an expression and report its elapsed time, like Stata's timer.

Usage

timer(x, on_error = TRUE)

Arguments

x

An expression to evaluate and time.

on_error

If TRUE (the default), also report elapsed time when the expression fails, then let the original error propagate. Use FALSE to report elapsed time only on success.

Value

The evaluated result, invisibly.

Details

The expression is evaluated once. On success, elapsed time is emitted as a message. Warnings and errors propagate normally. When the expression fails (or is interrupted) and on_error = TRUE, a message marked as failed execution reports the elapsed time while the error unwinds; the original condition object, including its call, is not modified.

Nested or repeated timers each measure everything evaluated inside them, so a later timer in a pipeline reports cumulative time from its own start.

See also

Other utility functions: capture(), set_seed()

Examples

x <- seq_len(1e6)
mean(x) |> timer()
#> Time spent: 0.013s

try(timer(stop("failure")))
#> Failed execution. Time spent: 0.000s
#> Error in timer(stop("failure")) : failure
